jobs.name: Undergrid — Pump Gallery and Relay Hall
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE complete new playable-map CONCEPT IMAGE for the owner's approval. This is a composition painting, not a sprite atlas, not runtime assets, not a finished game screenshot with UI.
Input images 1 and 2 are the approved PawTrail Neon Heights arrival and market concepts. Match their exact detailed textured 2D pixel-art medium, muted low-key values, fine dark colored contours, upper-left material highlights, graphite construction, cyan/magenta accents and warm amber work lights. Carry their world identity into a genuinely different utility district. No medieval buildings.
Camera: elevated top-down three-quarter orthographic RPG map, aligned to horizontal/vertical native walking axes, visible fronts and tops, NOT diamond-isometric and NOT cinematic perspective. The whole map in one landscape image, no cropping of entry/exit destinations. Consistent actor scale: a tiny adult about 40 native pixels tall within a roughly 1280-pixel-wide map; industrial doors generously taller than this actor. Don't make characters the focal point.
Ground: continuous quiet weathered surfaces with authored connected paths, no editor square grid, obvious tile seams, checkerboard, cursor, HUD, frames, captions, arrows, labels, logos, watermark or readable painted text. Local lamps and machine panels are part of the environment, not floating screen UI. Every primary destination needs a broad safe standing approach; maintain a clear return route. Route geometry should read immediately from the painting.
Show separable moving parts in a single sharp instant: fan rotors, emissive segments, small vent/light effects, holographic scan layers. Structures and the ground remain fixed; no motion blur or giant glow fog. Cyberpunk but grounded and slightly worn, with restrained colored reflections. Full opaque background.
Primary request: envision UNDERGRID, a 40×28-tile (1280×896 native) maintenance district beneath the neon streets. Cutaway overhead architecture leaves the playable floor completely visible. It is a connected utility gallery, not a glossy spaceship, sewer sludge maze or giant boss arena.
Composition: lower-left/southwest is the return hatch to Lumen Market, surrounded by a small clearly safe landing with warm light. An unobstructed main lane bends from there around a central machinery island to the upper-right/northeast service lift leading up to Rainline Skybridge. The transit walkway is all one physical ground plane; decorative coolant troughs are physically bounded with clear walkable bypasses, not implied jump platforms.
Western half: the Pump Gallery has two large ribbed pump drums, curved graphite/copper pipes and a contained teal coolant reservoir. A small readable harvest valve sits at the reservoir edge with an accessible dry approach. Nearby service vents form a clearly delimited hazard pocket with striped hardware and safe waiting spaces; no warning overlays, just physical stripes and lamps. One small hovering robot-wisp silhouette in the pocket suggests a bounded encounter, separated from the return landing.
Eastern/northern half: Relay Hall is an open workshop alcove with a prominent weathered three-by-three relay board/terminal, visible individual conduits, one supply cabinet on each side and ample clear floor in front. Use nine inset hardware modules rather than a floating game UI screen. The service lift is distinct and visible beyond the alcove at upper right.
A second compact patrol pocket at lower-right has a small mechanical hound silhouette and a bypass lane. Props reinforce room stories without blocking the main corridor. Perimeter: thick support ribs, exposed cables, grated wall vents, a few amber maintenance lamps and deep indigo recesses. No roof covering the lane, no giant skyline inside, no crowded junk scatter, no NPC camp in the damage pocket.
Mood: cool utility indigo and desaturated metal, selective teal coolant and tiny magenta status segments, warm safe entries. Favor clear broad maintenance corridors and readable pockets over a dense labyrinth. Full-map concept D.

Primary request: envision RAINLINE SKYBRIDGE, a 40×24-tile (1280×768 native) elevated cyberpunk maintenance walkway connecting the Undergrid to the future freight switchyard. Although physically high above the city, every playable platform and route in THIS map is a single continuous plane with solid railings. No jumping, disconnected ledges or ambiguous traversable elevation.
Composition: broad irregular left-to-right service promenade with one side loop. Lower-left/west is the warm-lit Undergrid service lift arrival and safe waiting bay. Far-right/east is a clear walled stair/gate threshold leading toward the future switchyard; it remains visually a destination beyond this map rather than a second map painted into the scene. The main route bends between two distinct industrial patrol pockets with safe alcoves and a readable way back.
Left-of-center/north side: Nyx's safe courier shelter is a compact burgundy/slate cloth awning, worn bench, clipped route cards, parcel shelf and small amber work lamp, tucked behind a protective half-wall. A tiny neutral courier silhouette with a weatherproof short coat and satchel stands in the safe alcove, facing the open approach. No portrait or romantic/flirty pose. The shelter is physically separated from the combat lane.
Upper-right/center-right: the Signal Archive is a restrained sealed charcoal service kiosk with a cyan projection display, four small symbol-shaped hardware lights (fish, moon, fish, star) hinting at the memory-sequence puzzle, and a separate small locker and nearby readable-shape maintenance plaque. No written puzzle solution or legible words. Keep standing space in front and the optional locker separate from the quest terminal.
Two modest hostile-machine silhouettes establish short patrol pockets: a low riveted mechanical hound near the middle-left lane and one slim security robot near the mid-right lane. Neither is giant or part of a monster crowd; avoid drawing beams or hit overlays. Rails and small machinery create deliberate bypass/waiting pockets rather than trapping the courier.
Background beyond the solid north/south rails: distant lower-value cyan/magenta city facades, cables and rain haze; keep these dim and subordinate so the foreground walkway reads. Place a few fans, amber service lamps, tiny rotating-ready sign mechanisms and translucent koi-like signal light details as separable scenery; no huge hologram covering paths. Wet slate flooring has subtle localized reflections and irregular wear, not repeated square tile edges. No cars on the pedestrian path or extra unrequested districts.
Mood: exposed but inhabited, cool rainline blues with protective amber shelter, fine textured pixel rendering. Full-map concept E.
